player_data.basis: 1681 of 15488 rated players have production the feed attributed in some season this build read (0 in the current season so far); the rest are on the roster with no attributed event anywhere, and are rated at positional replacement with a low confidence that says so

recruiting.basis: no legal, public, keyless recruiting feed is wired in — every path in cfbfastR-data 404s and CollegeFootballData requires a per-user key whose terms forbid redistributing the data as a committed dataset. The adapter exists and the fields stay null rather than being invented.

production.basis: 8 of 12 attribution columns cleared their coverage floor this season

availability.basis: 0 live availability records across FBS after 5 stale reports were discarded. College football has no universal injury report and this number will never reach 1.

scheme.basis: measured tendencies only. Personnel, concepts, coverage shells, blitz rate and box counts are not carried by any public feed and are never counted as measured.

quality.basis: the unweighted mean of the five dimensions. Recruiting sits at zero and drags the overall down on purpose: a research layer that scored itself only on what it happens to have would be marking its own homework.

snap_share.reason: no public college feed publishes snap counts. Box-score APPEARANCES are now ingested and are direct participation evidence, but an appearance is not a snap and is never called one.

pressures.reason: a hurry is ESPN’s own charting judgement rather than a tracked event, so it is a pressure PROXY — but it is a real observation and it is no longer treated as absent. Usable from 2024; gated per season.

tackles.reason: usable from 2024 at 62-65 per team-game; before that the column is barely filled in and fails its gate

tackles_for_loss.reason: usable from 2024 at 5.3 per team-game. The closest public thing to a run stop, and it is labelled as that rather than as one.

run_stops.reason: a run stop is a tackle at or behind the line-to-gain by DOWN AND DISTANCE, and no public feed joins a tackle to the play state. Tackles for loss are ingested as the nearest observable relative and are not renamed.

missed_tackles.reason: not carried in any public feed. A tackling-efficiency measure remains impossible and is not approximated.

coverage_targets.reason: no defender is attributed to a target, so completion rate allowed still cannot be computed per player. Passes defended ARE now observed and are a different, narrower thing.

ol_individual.reason: no public feed attributes a block, a pressure allowed or a run lane to a named lineman. This remains the largest genuine gap in the layer.

yards_after_contact.reason: not carried in any public college feed

recruiting_rating.reason: no legal, public, keyless recruiting feed is wired in — every path in cfbfastR-data 404s and CollegeFootballData requires a per-user key whose terms forbid redistributing the data as a committed dataset. The adapter exists and the fields stay null rather than being invented.

epa.reason: the play-attribution table carries no next-score information, and the expected-points surface this repo once fitted is no longer reproducible from public files. Success rate, explosive rate and yards per play are measured directly instead of an EPA being invented.

punting.reason: punting has been observable in every season checked (4.1-4.8 punts per team-game) and was wrongly declared absent. Punters are now rateable.

targets.reason: target attribution in the play table has season-scale coverage collapses; gated per season

interceptions.reason: interception attribution has season-scale coverage collapses; gated per season in both feeds

pass_breakups.reason: the play table’s break-up column collapses by season; the player box carries passes defended reliably from 2024 and is preferred where both exist

forced_fumbles.reason: forced-fumble attribution has season-scale coverage collapses; gated per season

qbr.reason: ESPN’s adjusted QBR is ingested and shown as CONTEXT, and is deliberately NOT an input to any EdgeDesk rating. It is another organisation’s model output, and this repo’s standing rule is that no rating of ours is built on somebody else’s rating.

candidates.basis: EPIR v1 remains canonical. The v2 candidate exists beside it and is promoted only by the walk-forward in football/validation/.

detail_note: Per-player detail, the full scheme profile and each unit’s projected participants live in football/players/teams/<team key>.json and are loaded on demand. This manifest is the league-wide view and is deliberately small enough to load on every page open.
notes: Every number here is arithmetic over counted events. No language model produced, adjusted or reviewed any rating in this file.
Snap counts do not exist in any public college feed. Role and participation are derived from TOUCH share and are labelled as such everywhere.
An offensive lineman cannot be rated individually by anything public. His unit is rated from the team’s own observed sack rate and stuff rate allowed, and the file says so.
A missing input contributes nothing and lowers confidence. It is never replaced by a league average.
